This has everything needed for professional engineering journals from easy diagram creation with shape and ruler tools via Apple Pencil to textboxes, pdf, and image editing. It even works with auto backups to webdav allowing users to backup their vital documents to their own private servers securely or just google drive or icloud for simplicity. The lifetime purchase option is the only reason I paid fulled price for the upgrade to support the developers when I could have opted for a discount. While being an almost perfect app, I still use Joplin for rich text language based documents useful for wikis, papers, and reports. Being able to create notes in the .html format so that the text shifts with window scaling is still a must have in the realm of technical multitasking on screens.

reviews.title: GO TO A DIFFERENT APP
reviews.text:
I genuinely regret using this app. I started the free trial to see if it was worth paying for, only to find out that the free version limits you to 3 folders. I created 2 additional folders during my subscription, and once it expired, I could no longer write in ANY of my folders. I lost access to notes I had already taken, which is ridiculous.

And that’s not even the worst part. This app attempted to charge me 8 TIMES for nearly $15 just to take basic notes that honestly look cheaper than notes I could write on paper. They advertise that you can cancel your subscription whenever you want, yet I couldn’t even find a way to cancel it properly.

The fact that they attempted to charge me 8 times is absolutely ridiculous. This entire experience has been frustrating, and I feel like this app cares more about getting your money than providing a good service.

Nearly $15 just to write notes and organize them into folders? I could literally do the same thing on paper for free without worrying about losing access to my own work.

Save yourself the headache and find a different note-taking app. There are better options out there, and I would NOT recommend wasting your time or money on this one.

reviews.title: Overheating and Lag Issues
reviews.text:
Using the infinite canvas for my note taking whilst studying and despite only filling maybe 1-2% of the entire canvas, my iPad immediately starts to get hot enough to fry an egg, battery drains fast and writing lag makes it virtually unusable! 

This happens whenever my notes get beyond a certain size, but it’s by no means excessive! I’ve adjusted all settings but nothing makes a difference, I also start getting rendering issues where text starts to disappear one by one before eventually reappearing.  Quitting and reloading restores the text but still instantly starts lagging and overheating.  

I’ve started my studies on this app so the cost of switching is time consuming but I’ll have to try another app as I can’t continue the next 500 hours of study with this issue, which seems to be something other people have also experienced.  

I’m using an M3 iPad Air so shouldn’t be having this sort of issue with a writing programme!

I’ve contacted tech support but no one has bothered to respond for weeks! So they obviously don’t care about their customers and are happy to keep making money off of a broken product.  I can’t see how such an issue could not be known about and fixed, as this is software build for iPad OS so surely the developers have tested their product? But no sign they are fixing the issue, which seems to have been known in the community for years now!

I don’t recommend anyone download this product until the developers fix it, because it’s currently broken and unus

reviews.title: App needs work.  Not intuitive at all
reviews.text: I give credit to the Goodnotes people because they reached out to me in response to my previous critical review.  Unfortunately, the answer was to read voluminous articles and instruction manuals.  This is not going to happen.  I need the app to be intuitive so that a genius like me can use the app without reading tons of material.  I have great expertise running all sorts of apps and I agree that some apps should be subject to expertise that is gained through reading manuals.  For crying out loud, this is a NOTES app!  It should be simple.  I was told that I could use it to record all of the information that I need about photographs I take with vintage film cameras.  Digital cameras do this all automatically, but I shoot film which means that I need a simple app to record all the data for each shot I take like: Film type, format, shutter speed, aperture, exposure index, atmospheric conditions, zone system offsets, developer push/pull recommendation, etc.  This app is not it.  It is hard enough for me to figure out all the camera settings I need to take the perfect shot.  It is critical that I be able to document all of the factors that make up the perfect shot so that I can apply the same principles to future images.  To do this, I need a good Notes App that is easy to use that I do not need to divert my intellect away from applying it to my photography.  This app ain’t it.

reviews.title: Appalling Ease of Use for a 75-Year-Old Lifetime “Special Edition” User
reviews.text:
I am a paying lifetime “Special Edition” user who purchased Goodnotes through the Apple App Store on 6 September 2023.

I appreciate the power and design of the application, but I must honestly express disappointment regarding accessibility and usability for older users and people with cognitive or visual difficulties.

I am using the latest iPad Pro 13” M5 (2025), so the issues I describe are not related to outdated hardware.

Despite paying for the premium lifetime “Special Edition” version through the App Store, basic accessibility and reading features still appear to be missing, including:

• Infinite scrolling text
• Automatic text reflow when increasing font sizes
• Zoom lock or protection against accidental zooming
• Easier adaptive page rendering
• Simpler document handling for elderly and disabled users

At 75 years old, with eyesight difficulties and ADHD, I find it extremely frustrating that enlarging text for readability often breaks the layout of the page and forces constant manual adjustment of zoom and formatting.

Modern note-taking applications should adapt to the user — especially paying users — rather than requiring constant technical management of page rendering and scaling.

Many elderly users are now purchasing high-end iPads specifically for reading, note-taking, memory support, study, and accessibility purposes. Yet Goodnotes still behaves more like rigid digital paper than an adaptive modern reading environment.

I’ve been using it for the better part of 3 years now

But the writing experience is unusable, I’ve had to get other apps simply because when I want to annotate or hand write notes, it’s like it has a mind of its own. I’ve turned stroke stabilisation
down to zero but still at the end of letters the writing changes direction. I’ve been using Notability for handwritten notes and do not have this issue, which is a shame because it means I can’t have everything in one place.

reviews.title: Great app but one main issue about battery and overheating
reviews.text: Over the past 6 months I’ve been using Goodnotes extensively, for more than 8 hours a day at certain points. There’s lots I’ve loved, from the different options of pens and papers to use as well as how simple it is to upload files to write and annotate over. However, this week I’ve had to switch over to Noteful and the reason behind this is entirely due to what I believe is optimisation issues within the app. While writing on my Ipad, my screen starts heating up almost instantly to the point where it starts becoming painful to touch. It also has been eating away at my battery health, where an IPad I brought at the beginning of the year has dropped in battery health to 88% despite being brand new less than 6 months ago. This is a massive issue as a few days ago it began heating up so much to the point where my IPad stopped charging completely, even after I had closed the app. I am unsure why a note taking app does require so much battery but due to this I have had to switch to alternatives as it continues to degrade my Ipad and I worry that one day it will just crash and I will lose all work I have been going through. Should Goodnotes fix these overheating and battery issues I’d love to come back as other note taking apps can’t compete but sadly for the time being the issue is to large to tolerate any longer :(

reviews.text: I loved this app before the update. I bought it a couple months ago and paid for it. I was using the free version before and loved it so I decided to buy the lifetime version. About a week later it got this absolutely HORRENDOUS update it’s really infuriating. There was no need for a floating tool bar as the tools being at the top was much more convenient and out the way and iPads have a tool bar at the bottom of the screen. reviews.title: Good until the update
reviews.text: I use the app for my uni notes and it’s so good for keeping modules separate and making notes that are easy to read and access again, however there was a big update which completely changed the toolbar, moving all the buttons for text editing, making it a challenge to use in lectures when all of a sudden everything had changed. Some pages are deleting my text input, so I could spend 20 mins writing up a page of notes, and then the app deletes itself. The text size buttons are also ridiculously unreliable, it seems to be that the button for whichever size I want to use (usually H2 and H3) just don’t seem to work, I just have to keep cycling through the sizes until it eventually lets me select the size I want to use, it can genuinely take up to 5 minutes at times. Highly disappointing for an app you have to pay to access properly, not sure if I’ll be using it again next year if i’m honest.
